source.title: On the Stability of Gradient Descent for Large Learning Rate

record.file_problem: Full text is present. The title in the supplied metadata differs slightly from the title in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves and experimentally illustrates that sufficiently large fixed learning rates can prevent convergence to minima for almost all initializations, qualifying claims about recovery at large learning rates.
record.gate_note: Results about cited prior work are not extracted. Figure 4 reports convergence percentages by depth and learning rate, but the supplied text does not state the plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study measures convergence of parameter trajectories to minima, whereas V5 concerns loss recovery, loss divergence, and sharpness dynamics relative to stability thresholds. Nonconvergence to a fixed minimum can coexist with bounded trajectories and falling loss. The discussion explicitly leaves divergence to infinity unresolved, so these results do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors prove almost-everywhere nonconvergence to minima above a threshold for linear networks with quadratic loss, extend this under additional assumptions, and present nonlinear-network experiments. Their result does not imply loss divergence. The discussion acknowledges that the nonlinear Hessian lower-bound assumption remains difficult to verify; the experiments illustrate the proposed behavior rather than establish that assumption.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies fixed-step gradient descent convergence to minima or critical points, rather than the recovery and loss trajectory described in V5; its experiments use MNIST networks and its main theorem concerns linear networks.
record.method_sensitivity: Convergence depends on learning rate; the experiments also vary network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: For linear networks with quadratic loss, Theorem 15 states that above a learning-rate threshold, initializations converging to a minimum form a measure-zero set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently large fixed learning rates prevent parameter convergence to minima for almost every initialization in the analyzed linear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports no convergent trajectories for η > 1 in the tested full-batch GELU/MSE MNIST networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large fixed learning rates can eliminate trajectory convergence in the tested nonlinear networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 4 reports convergence percentages across learning rates and depths for ReLU networks trained with SGD; individual values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trajectory-convergence frequency can be studied as a function of learning rate and depth under SGD.

record.problems: The experimental figures report convergence percentages but the supplied text gives few numerical values; the experiments use MNIST subsets rather than CIFAR benchmarks. Theoretical results concern convergence to minima and do not measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and the specified training recipes.
Spurious-minimum frequency and the benefit of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Loss recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, transient loss and curvature changes, divergence at larger rates or below the initial threshold, and sharpness hovering near the stability threshold while loss falls.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Neither supporting nor challenging V5 follows from failure of parameter convergence alone.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and the stated SGD/Adam recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks, spurious minima, and student width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth effects, shortcuts, and normalization.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth.

The paper does not test the initial linearized-model stability limit, a transient loss rise followed by low training loss, sharpness hovering at the stability threshold, or the stated wide-network setting.
Batch normalization comparisons, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

rows.subject: linear networks with quadratic loss
rows.operation_detail: Proves that for learning rates above a threshold, the set of initializations converging to a minimum has measure zero.
rows.measure: Whether gradient descent converges to a minimum
rows.value: The set of initializations that converge to a minimum has measure zero.
rows.note: The result concerns convergence to minima for linear networks with quadratic loss, not the catapult dynamics or a measured stability threshold.
rows.check: Theorem 15 establishes almost-everywhere nonconvergence to minima above an existential learning-rate threshold. It does not establish loss divergence or failure of the recovery described in V5. The theorem's result is accurately paraphrased, but its version link and state are inappropriate.
